synopsis: Data replay feeds recorded sensor data into braking software, while HIL runs a real control unit against a simulated machine; the glossary identifies HIL as the only way to test ECU timing and interfaces before the machine exists [f16032, f16042]. The booklet recommends an ISO/TS 21815-2-interface HIL bench for mid-2027, but keeping it off the critical path unless interfaces stabilize early; sensor injection is sensor- and ECU-specific, with raw-signal benches requiring the most integration effort [f16044, f16043]. Commercial alternatives span dSPACE, NI, Speedgoat and OPAL-RT, but the cited on-road replay/HIL evidence establishes architectural feasibility rather than suitability for this off-road manufacturer; OPAL-RT separately names off-highway and defense users [f8363, f8364, f5610, f9235]. An NI PXIe-8842 controller is listed at about USD 5,200, not a complete bench price; the NI system requires a quote, and no full-system dSPACE price was found [f8644, f9227, f8642].
